name: Classic Organic Aciduria

criteria.description: Presence of metabolic acidosis with elevated anion gap
Detection of elevated specific organic acids in urine by gas chromatography-mass spectrometry
Demonstration of deficient activity of specific mitochondrial enzymes involved in organic acid metabolism
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes encoding enzymes of organic acid metabolism
Presence of characteristic clinical features such as vomiting, lethargy, and developmental delay

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of metabolic acidosis with elevated anion gap plus detection of elevated organic acids in urine and demonstration of enzyme deficiency
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing supports diagnosis but is not mandatory if biochemical criteria are met.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe metabolic acidosis with elevated anion gap
searchTerms: dangerous blood acidity with elevated gap

pathognomonic.symptomName: Elevated urinary excretion of specific organic acids
searchTerms: high levels of organic acids in urine
abnormal organic acids found in urine

pathognomonic.symptomName: Enzyme deficiency in mitochondrial organic acid metabolism pathways
searchTerms: lack of mitochondrial organic acid enzymes

common.symptomName: Lethargy and decreased level of consciousness

laboratory: Increased urinary organic acids (e.g. methylmalonic acid, propionic acid)
imaging: Brain MRI may show basal ganglia lesions or delayed myelination
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes such as MUT, PCCB, or other mitochondrial enzyme genes
other: Enzymatic assays demonstrating deficient activity of specific organic acid metabolism enzymes

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of branched-chain ketoacids in urine
Different enzyme deficiencies affecting branched-chain amino acid metabolism
Marked hyperammonemia without significant organic aciduria
Normal or mildly elevated anion gap

redFlags: Rapid onset of metabolic acidosis with neurological deterioration
Failure to respond to standard metabolic acidosis treatment
Recurrent episodes of vomiting and lethargy in infancy
references: Saudubray JM, Garcia-Cazorla A. Inborn errors of metabolism overview: pathophysiology, manifestations, evaluation, and management. Pediatr Clin North Am. 2018;65(2):179-208.
